# README

Full rules, evidence and examples: `common/writing/repo-readme.md`.

- README-01 must: Build every repo README to one skeleton, in the order given under Good; library and client READMEs use README-10's middle; other deviations are decided per repo and noted in that repo.
  Good: H1, badge row, one-sentence intro (`This repository contains the infrastructure as code (IaC) for X using Pulumi.`), `---`, Requirements, Creating, Destroying, Environment Variables or Secrets, `---`, Configuration (one H3 per block), `---`, Continuous Integration and Automations, Development.
  Bad: a marketing paragraph before the purpose.
- README-02 prefer: Title homelab repos `Homelab: <Area> - <Part>` and other repos with the plain product name; add no tagline.
- README-03 must: Put a row of `style=for-the-badge` badges directly under the H1, followed by a blank line and the intro: shields.io badges, except the OpenSSF Scorecard badge, which comes from `api.scorecard.dev`; a support button such as Buy Me a Coffee may sit in the row.
  Good: H1, then the `for-the-badge` row (shields.io badges plus the Scorecard badge from `api.scorecard.dev`), a blank line, then the intro.
  Bad: badges after the intro, or default-style badges.
- README-04 prefer: In IaC READMEs, separate major blocks with `---` on its own line, not between every H2; library and client READMEs may use `---` before Development and Contributors.
- README-05 must: In Requirements, name and link mise in one line and nothing else. Open the Development section with one sentence: tool versions (list them) are managed with mise, without a second link; run `mise trust` and `mise install` once, then use the usual commands (list them).
  Good: Requirements has `- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev)`; Development opens with `Tool versions (Go, golangci-lint, Pulumi) are managed with mise: run \`mise trust\` and \`mise install\` once, then use \`make lint\`.`
  Bad: per-tool download links in Requirements.
- README-06 must: End IaC and config READMEs with "Continuous Integration and Automations" (two bullets, GitHub Actions and Renovate Bot), then Development.
  Good: a section "Continuous Integration and Automations", followed by Development, with `- GitHub Actions: lint and deploy on push` and `- Renovate Bot: updates images and actions`.
  Bad: CI details scattered through the README with no closing section.
- README-07 must: In IaC and config READMEs, document each configuration key in a `yaml` block whose values are the descriptions, mirroring the structure, one H3 per top-level key, with no table; suffix `(optional, default: X)` and `(e.g. ...)` in that order, and put units in the description (`in s`, `in ms`, `in %`).
  Good: `### vault` over `address: the vault url (e.g. https://vault.example.org)` and `timeout: request timeout in s (optional, default: 30)`.
  Bad: a Markdown table of keys and descriptions.
- README-08 must: List environment variables as `- \`NAME\`: the lowercase description`, grouped by provider, not in a table.
  Good: ``- `API_TOKEN`: the api token of the provider``.
  Bad: a table with columns Name and Description.
- README-09 prefer: In IaC READMEs, open a Configuration section that holds secrets with a bold-italic `***Attention:***` line pointing to the tool's secret encryption; library READMEs may use plain `**Attention**:`.
- README-10 prefer: Library and client READMEs replace README-01's middle with Installation, Configuration (a table with Option and Description), Usage and Development, in that order; a library without options has no Configuration section; README-07's no-table rule does not apply to them.
- README-11 prefer: Add Contributors and Supporting sections (including generated all-contributors blocks and support text) only to published open-source projects, never to private repos.
